# Incident Report — Network Traffic Analysis

**Case:** MTA 2024-11-26 traffic-analysis-exercise
**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 frames), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.png`

## 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** | Consistent source of all malicious traffic below |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP replies and Ethernet frames for 10.11.26.183 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS name registrations (`<00>`, `<20>`) and NTLMSSP `auth.hostname` field |
| Windows domain | NEMOTODES / AD domain `nemotoads.health` (DC: NEMOTODE-DC, 10.11.26.3) | NBNS, DNS SRV lookups for `_ldap._tcp...nemotoads.health` |
| Logged-in user account | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3) |

## 2. Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client).

**Attribution basis: both signature-confirmed and behaviorally corroborated.**
- **Signature-confirmed:** Suricata/ET alerts fired directly on the traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- **Behaviorally corroborated in the pcap itself:** the HTTP `User-Agent` on every outbound C2 POST is literally `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, and the POST bodies to `/fakeurl.htm` decode to the NetSupport client-server protocol verbs `CMD\nPOLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1` (initial handshake/poll) and `CMD\nENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<binary>` (encrypted command channel), which is the documented wire format for this RAT. The client also performed a geolocation lookup to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (`GET /location/loca.asp`), a known artifact of NetSupport client initialization.

## 3. Timeline / infection chain (all times relative to capture start)

1. **t≈32-38s** — Host resolves and connects to two lookalike domains associated with a fake "cracked APK/mod" download site: `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) and `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139). Suricata flagged `modandcrackedapk.com` under signature `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and again `... in TLS SNI`, indicating a known malicious redirect/delivery domain. These sessions carried several MB of TLS-encrypted data (largest: 5.7 MB over 193.42.38.139:443) — content not recoverable from this capture (genuine TLS, no plaintext, no server certificate captured in the visible handshake).
2. **t≈67s** — Immediately after that download activity, 10.11.26.183 begins beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** with `POST /fakeurl.htm`, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` — the NetSupport RAT C2 checking in. This is consistent with the downloaded payload from step 1 being the RAT installer/dropper.
3. **t≈67s** — GET `/location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) — RAT client geolocation self-check.
4. **t=67s through end of capture (~3050s / ~51 min)** — Persistent C2 beaconing every ~60 seconds to 194.180.191.64:443 (`fakeurl.htm`), alternating `POLL` and `ENCD` command frames — classic remote-access-trojan keepalive/command-channel behavior.
5. Supporting DNS resolution to `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207) appears in the same window and is likely part of the same delivery/redirect chain (ad/redirect gate typically used ahead of fake download pages), though no direct malicious payload transfer through it was captured in plaintext.

## 4. Indicators of Compromise (grounded in captured traffic)

**Command-and-control:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — primary NetSupport RAT C2 (HTTP-over-443, plaintext, `POST /fakeurl.htm`). Two client sessions observed: source ports 53362 (67s–2977s) and 53500 (3050s onward, capture ends mid-session).
- `104.26.1.231:80` — `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, RAT geolocation service (`GET /location/loca.asp`).

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 (ET CURRENT_EVENTS "ZPHP Domain" — DNS lookup and TLS SNI)
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5
- `confirmsubscription.com` → 52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 (RAT-associated infrastructure, not inherently malicious domain but confirms RAT presence)

**Malicious URLs (observed in plaintext HTTP):**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (repeated POST, C2 beacon/command channel)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp`

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- No malware binary (EXE/MSI/DLL/script) was transferred in plaintext HTTP within this capture — the only HTTP object transfers observed are benign/incidental (`connecttest.txt`, Microsoft OCSP response, `ProcessMAU.txt` from `acroipm2.adobe.com`, Windows CTL `.cab` updates). The likely payload delivery to the host occurred inside the encrypted TLS sessions to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139) and `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5); **no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this evidence** since that traffic is genuinely encrypted and no certificate or file metadata was recoverable from the capture. Do not report a hash for this incident — none is observable.

## 5. Other alerts noted, assessed as not directly tied to this RAT infection
- SMBv1/NTLMSSP/`MS-EFSR EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` alerts between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3) reflect normal (if legacy/insecure) Windows domain-authentication and file-share protocol chatter on this LAN; nothing in the capture links them to the NetSupport RAT's actions (no lateral-movement traffic from 10.11.26.183 to other LAN hosts was observed).

## 6. Recommended actions
- Isolate 10.11.26.183 (DESKTOP-B8TQK49) from the network immediately.
- Block outbound to 194.180.191.64:443, 193.42.38.139, 213.246.109.5, 104.26.1.231/geo.netsupportsoftware.com at the perimeter.
- Reset credentials for domain account `oboomwald`.
- Perform host forensics on DESKTOP-B8TQK49 to recover the actual NetSupport RAT client binary/config (client32.exe / client32.ini equivalents) for hashing, since the dropper content was not recoverable from network evidence alone.
